evidence.excerpt: Smart building automation systems increasingly integrate heterogeneous controllers managing heating, ventilation, access control, and fire suppression, all connected over IP-based networks. This convergence introduces significant attack surfaces that are rarely addressed through systematic security engineering. This paper applies a structured threat modelling methodology—adapted from STRIDE and augmented with ICS-specific threat categories—to a representative smart building controller architecture. The analysis identifies seventeen distinct threat scenarios spanning spoofing of sensor inputs, tampering with actuator commands, and denial-of-service against building management gateways. For each threat, the paper proposes corresponding mitigations including cryptographic command authentication, rate-limiting policies, and network segmentation strategies. A comparative evaluation against an unmitigated baseline system is conducted using a simulation environment, demonstrating measurable risk reduction across all identified threat categories. The findings offer actionable security guidance for building automation vendors and facility managers deploying next-generation smart infrastructure.
